translations.text: After Moses, the servant of the Lord, died, the Lord said to Joshua son of Nun, Moses’ assistant:
Moses my servant is dead. Now get up and cross this Jordan, you and all these people, into the land that I am giving them, the Israelites.
Every place where the sole of your foot treads will be yours, as I told Moses.

From the wilderness and this mountain of Lebanon as far as the Euphrates, the great river, including all the land of the Hittites, and as far as the Great Sea toward the setting sun—this will be your territory.
No one will be able to stand against you all the days of your lives. Just as I was with Moses, I will also be with you. I will not abandon you or leave you.
Be strong and very courageous, because you will give these people as their inheritance the land that I swore to their ancestors to give them.

Only be strong and very courageous, taking care to obey all the laws that Moses my servant commanded you. Do not turn away from them to the right or to the left, so that you may succeed wherever you go.
This book of the law must not leave your mouth. Instead, meditate on it night and day, and take care to do everything written in it, so that you may prosper and succeed.
Look, I have commanded you: be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or tremble, because the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.
Joshua commanded the leaders of the people and their scribes, saying to them:

Go through the camp and command the people, telling them, ‘Prepare provisions for yourselves, because three days from now you will cross this Jordan to enter and take possession of the land that the Lord your God is giving you to possess.’
Joshua said to Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh:
Remember the command that Moses, the Lord’s servant, gave you when he said to you, ‘The Lord your God is giving you rest and is giving you this land.’

Your wives, your families, and your livestock are to remain in the land that Moses gave you beyond the Jordan. But you, all your mighty warriors, are to cross over armed ahead of your brothers and help them,

until the Lord gives your brothers rest as he has given you, and they too take possession of the land that the Lord your God is giving them. Then you may return to the land of your inheritance and possess it, the land that Moses, the Lord’s servant, gave you beyond the Jordan, toward the rising sun.
The descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the descendants of Manasseh answered Joshua, ‘We will do everything you command us, and we will go wherever you send us.
Just as we obeyed Moses, so we will obey you. Only may the Lord your God be with you as he was with Moses.
Anyone who defies you and does not obey your word in everything you command him is to be put to death. Only be strong and courageous.’

Joshua son of Nun sent two men familiar with the land from Shittim and told them, ‘Go and examine the land of Jericho.’ They went and entered the house of a prostitute named Rahab and spent the night there.
The king of Jericho was told, ‘Look, some Israelite men have come here tonight to spy out the land.’
The king of Jericho sent word to Rahab, telling her, ‘Bring out the men who came to you tonight, because they have come to spy out our land.’
The woman took the two men and hid them. She said, ‘The men did indeed come to me, but I did not know where they were from.
When it was time to close the gate in the evening, they left, and I do not know where they went. Go after them quickly, because you will catch up with them.’
But she had taken them up to the roof and hidden them among the flax stalks she had laid out on the roof.
The men went after them along the road to the Jordan, toward the ford. The gate was closed after the pursuers had gone out after those spies.
They had not yet lain down when she went up to them on the roof.
She said to the men, ‘I know that the Lord has handed the land over to you. Fear of you has fallen upon us, and all the inhabitants of the land are afraid of you.
For we have heard how the Lord dried up the waters of the Red Sea before you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites, Sihon and Og, whom you destroyed.
When we heard this, our hearts trembled, and no courage remained in any of us because of you. For the Lord your God is God in heaven above and on earth below.
Now swear to me by the Lord that, because I have shown you kindness, you too will show kindness to me and my father’s household. Give me a trustworthy sign.
and spare my father, my mother, my brothers, my sisters, and everyone belonging to us, and save our lives from death.”
The men said to her, “We give our own lives to die in your place, provided you do not reveal this matter. When the Lord gives us this land, we will show you kindness and faithfulness.”
She lowered them by a rope through the window, because her house was built into the city wall, and she lived on the wall.
She said to them, “Go into the mountains, into the mountains, so that those who went out after you do not encounter you. Hide there for three days, until they return, and then go on your way.”
The men said to her, “We are free from this oath that you have made us swear.

“Look, when we enter the land, tie this scarlet cord in the window through which you lowered us. Bring your father, your mother, your brothers, and all your father’s household into the house with you.

Anyone who goes outside through the door of your house will have his blood on his own head, and we will be free of responsibility for him. But anyone who is with you inside the house will have his blood on our heads, and we will be responsible for him if anyone harms him.”
If you reveal this matter, we will be free from the oath that you have made us swear.”
She said to them, “Let it be as you have said.” She sent them away, and they left. Then she tied the scarlet cord in the window.

They went into the mountains and stayed there for three days, until those who had gone after them returned to the town. Those who had gone out after them searched for them along the whole road, and when they did not find them,
they returned. The two spies came down from the mountains, crossed over, and went to Joshua son of Nun. They told him everything that had happened to them.
They said to Joshua, “The Lord has handed the whole land over to us, and all the inhabitants of the land are afraid of us.”
Joshua rose early in the morning. They set out from Shittim, and all the people of Israel came to the Jordan. They spent the night there and did not cross over.
After three days, the officers went through the camp.
They instructed the people, saying to them, “When you see the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, and the priests and Levites carrying it, then set out from your place and follow it.
There must be a distance of about two thousand cubits between you and the ark. Do not approach it, so that you may know the way you should go, because you have never traveled this way before.”
Joshua said to the people, “Make yourselves holy, because tomorrow the Lord will do wonders among you.”
Joshua said to the priests, “Take up the ark of the covenant and go ahead of the people.” They took up the ark of the covenant and went ahead of the people.
The Lord said to Joshua, “Today I will begin to make you great in the eyes of all Israel, so that they may know that just as I was with Moses, I will also be with you.
Instruct the priests who carry the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and tell them, ‘When you reach the edge of the waters of the Jordan, stand there in the Jordan itself.’”
Joshua said to the Israelites, “Come here and hear the words of the Lord your God.”

Joshua said, “By this you will know that the living God is among you and will destroy before you the Hittites, the Canaanites, the Hivites, the Perizzites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, and the Jebusites.
Look, the ark of the covenant of the Lord, the Lord of the whole earth, is ahead of you in the Jordan.
Now choose twelve men for yourselves from all the tribes of Israel, one man from each tribe.

When the soles of the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord, the Lord of all the earth, rest in the waters of the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan will be divided. The waters flowing down from above will stand on one side, as though in a single waterskin.”
When the people set out from their tents to cross the Jordan, the priests carrying the ark of the covenant went ahead of the people.
When those carrying the ark reached the Jordan, the feet of the priests carrying the ark dipped into the water’s edge. The Jordan was full from bank to bank throughout the harvest season.

The waters flowing down from above stopped. They stood on one side as though in a single waterskin, extending very far away from Aram, the town beside Zarethan. The waters flowing down toward the western sea, the Salt Sea, came to an end and were cut off. The people crossed opposite Jericho.

The priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord stood on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan and remained ready. All the people of Israel crossed on dry ground, until the entire people had finished crossing the Jordan.
When all the people had finished crossing the Jordan, the Lord said to Joshua,
“Choose twelve men for yourselves from the people, one man from each tribe.”

He instructed them, saying, “Take twelve stones for yourselves from here, from the middle of the Jordan, from beneath the priests’ feet. Prepare them, carry them across with you, and put them at the lodging place where you will spend the night.”
Joshua called the twelve men whom they had selected from the Israelites, one man from each tribe.
Joshua said to them, “Go ahead of the ark of the Lord your God into the middle of the Jordan, and let each man put a stone on his shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the Israelites,
so that this may be a sign among you. When your children ask you in the future, ‘What are these stones?’

tell them, ‘The waters of the Jordan were divided before the ark of the covenant of the Lord. When we crossed the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were divided.’ These stones will be a memorial to the Israelites forever.”

The Israelites did as Joshua had commanded them. They took twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, as the Lord had told Joshua, corresponding to the number of the tribes of Israel. They carried them across with them to their lodging place and left them there.
They set up the twelve stones they had taken from the middle of the Jordan, from beneath the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the covenant. They remain there to this day.

The priests carrying the ark stood in the middle of the Jordan until everything the Lord had commanded Joshua to tell the people had been completed, just as Moses had commanded Joshua. The people hurried across.
When all the people had completely crossed over, the ark of the Lord and the priests crossed over ahead of the people.
The descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh crossed over armed ahead of the Israelites, as Moses had told them.
Forty thousand armed men crossed over before the Lord for battle on the plain of Jericho.
On that day the Lord made Joshua great in the eyes of all Israel. They revered him as they had revered Moses, all the days of his life.
The Lord said to Joshua,
“Command the priests carrying the ark of the testimony to come up out of the Jordan.”
Joshua commanded the priests, saying to them, “Come up out of the Jordan.”

When the priests carrying the ark of the Lord’s covenant came up from the middle of the Jordan, and the soles of the priests’ feet rested on dry ground, the waters of the Jordan returned to their place and flowed over all its banks as before.
The people came up from the middle of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month and camped at Gilgal, on the eastern outskirts of Jericho.
Joshua set up at Gilgal the twelve stones they had taken from the middle of the Jordan.
He said to the Israelites, “When your children ask you in the future, ‘What are these stones?’”
show them to your children and tell them, ‘The Israelites crossed this Jordan on dry ground.’
“The Lord your God dried up the waters of the Jordan before them until they had crossed, just as the Lord your God did to the Red Sea, which he dried up before us until we had crossed.”
“So that all the peoples of the earth may know that the hand of the Lord is mighty, and that you may fear the Lord your God always.”

When all the kings of the Amorites west of the Jordan and all the kings of Canaan along the sea heard that the Lord had dried up the waters of the Jordan before the Israelites until they had crossed, their hearts trembled, and no courage remained in them because of the Israelites.
At that time the Lord said to Joshua, “Make yourself a flint knife and circumcise the Israelites again, a second time.”
Joshua made himself a flint knife and circumcised the Israelites a second time at the Hill of the Foreskins.
These are the ones Joshua circumcised: all the male offspring of the people who had come out of Egypt, because all the fighting men had died in the wilderness along the way after coming out of Egypt.
For all the people who came out had been circumcised, but none of the people born in the wilderness along the way after they came out of Egypt had been circumcised.

For the Israelites traveled in the wilderness for forty years, until all the fighting men who had come out of Egypt had perished, because they had not obeyed the Lord their God. The Lord swore to them that he would not let them see the land he had sworn to their ancestors to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
Joshua circumcised their sons who came after them, because they were uncircumcised and had not been circumcised.
When all the people had finished being circumcised, they stayed in their places in the camp until they had healed.
The Lord said to Joshua, “Today I have removed from you the disgrace of the Egyptians.” He named that place Gilgal, as it is called to this day.
The Israelites camped at Gilgal and celebrated the Passover on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month, in the plain of Jericho.
After the Passover they ate some of the grain of the land. On that very day they ate unleavened bread and roasted grain.
The manna ceased the day after they ate the grain of the land. There was no more manna for the Israelites, and that year they ate the produce of the land of Canaan.
When Joshua was in the plain of Jericho, he looked up and saw a man standing opposite him, holding a drawn sword in his hand. Joshua went to him and said, “Are you one of us or one of our enemies?”
He said to him, “I am the commander of the Lord’s armies, and now I have come.” Joshua fell facedown on the ground, bowed in worship, and said, “What does my lord say to his servant?”
The commander of the Lord’s armies said to Joshua, “Take your sandals off your feet, because the place where you are standing is holy.” And Joshua did so.
Jericho was shut up because of the Israelites. No one went out, and no one came in.
The Lord said to Joshua, “See, I have handed Jericho over to you, along with its king and its entire army.
“March around the city, all you fighting men. Go around the city once each day. Do this for six days.”
“Seven priests shall carry horns and sound them before the ark. On the seventh day, go around the city seven times, and the priests shall blow the horns.”

“When they sound the horns and you hear the sound of the horn, all the people shall give a great shout. The city wall will fall down where it stands, and the people shall go up, each one straight ahead.”
Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said to them, “Carry the ark of the Lord’s covenant, and let seven priests carry seven horns and sound them before the ark of the Lord.”
He said to the people, “Go forward and march around the city, and let those who are armed go ahead of the ark of the Lord.”
As Joshua had told the people, seven priests carried seven horns and sounded blasts before the ark of the Lord. They blew the horns, and the ark of the Lord’s covenant followed them.
The armed men went ahead of the priests who were blowing the horns, and the rear guard followed the ark. They marched and blew the horns.
Joshua commanded the people, saying, “Do not shout or let your voices be heard. Do not let a word come out of your mouths until the day I tell you to shout. Then you shall shout.”
The ark of the Lord went around the city once. Then they returned to the camp and spent the night there.
Joshua rose early in the morning, and the priests took up the ark of the Lord.

Seven priests carried seven horns and went ahead of the ark of the Lord, marching and blowing the horns. The armed men went ahead of them, and the rear guard followed the ark of the Lord, blowing the horns.
On the second day they went around that city once and returned to the camp. They did this for all six days.
On the seventh day they rose early at dawn and went around the city seven times in this same manner. Only on that day did they go around it seven times.
On the seventh time, the priests blew the horns, and Joshua said to the people, “Shout, because the Lord has handed the city over to you!
This city and everything in it shall be devoted to the Lord for destruction. Only spare Rahab the prostitute and everyone with her in the house, because she hid the spies we sent.
But you must beware of the things devoted to destruction, so that you do not hide and take any of them, making the camp of Israel itself subject to destruction and bringing trouble upon it.
All the silver and gold, and the bronze and iron articles, are holy to the Lord. They shall go into the Lord’s treasury.”

The people shouted, and the horns were blown. When the people heard the sound of the horns, they gave a very loud shout, and the wall collapsed where it stood. The people went up into the city, each one straight ahead, and captured it.
They destroyed everything in it, men and women, young and old, as well as cattle, sheep, and donkeys. They destroyed them with the sword.
Joshua said to the two men who had spied out the land, “Go into that prostitute’s house and bring the woman out of there, along with all that belongs to her, just as you swore to her.”
The spies went and brought out Rahab, her father, her mother, her brothers, and all that belonged to her. They brought out her entire family and settled them outside the camp of Israel.
They burned the city and everything in it. Only the gold, silver, and bronze and iron articles did they bring into the Lord’s treasury.

Joshua spared Rahab the prostitute, her father’s household, and all that belonged to her. She has lived among the Israelites to this day, because she hid the spies whom Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.

At that time Joshua swore an oath, saying, “Cursed before the Lord is the man who rises up and rebuilds this city, Jericho. At the cost of his firstborn he shall rebuild it, and at the cost of his youngest he shall set up its gates.”
The Lord was with Joshua, and his fame spread throughout the land.

The Israelites acted unfaithfully concerning the things devoted to destruction. Achar son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of the things devoted to destruction and hid them. The Lord’s anger burned against the Israelites.
Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is beside Beth-aven, east of Bethel. He told them, “Go up and spy out the land.” So the men went up and spied out Ai.
They returned to Joshua and said to him, “Do not let all the people go up. Let about two or three thousand men go up and destroy Ai. Do not send all the people, because they are few.”
About three thousand men from the people went up there, but they fled before the men of Ai.
The men of Ai killed thirty-six men of Israel. They pursued them from before the gate until they were routed, and struck them down. The people’s hearts trembled, and they became like water.
Joshua tore his clothes and fell facedown on the ground before the ark of the Lord until evening, along with the elders of Israel. They put dust on their heads.
Joshua said, “Alas, Lord God! Why did you bring this people across the Jordan to hand us over to the Amorites? If only we had been content to remain on the other side of the Jordan!
What can I say now that Israel has turned its back before its enemies?
The Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear about this. They will gather against us and wipe out our name from the face of the earth. What, then, will you do for your great name?”
The Lord said to Joshua, “Get up! Why are you lying face down on the ground?
Israel has sinned. They have violated the command I gave them, taken some of the things devoted to destruction, stolen, lied, and hidden them among their belongings.

The Israelites will no longer be able to stand against their enemies. Instead, they will turn their backs on their enemies, because they have become devoted to destruction. I will no longer be with them unless you remove the things devoted to destruction from among you.

Get up, prepare this people, and say, ‘Prepare yourselves for tomorrow, because this is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: There are things devoted to destruction among you, Israel. You can no longer stand against your enemies until you remove the things devoted to destruction from among you.’

In the morning, bring your tribes forward. The tribe the Lord selects shall come forward clan by clan. The clan the Lord selects shall come forward household by household, and the household the Lord selects shall come forward man by man.
Whoever is caught with the things devoted to destruction shall be burned with fire, he and everything he has, because he violated the Lord’s command and committed wrongdoing in Israel.
Joshua rose early in the morning and brought Israel forward tribe by tribe, and the tribe of Judah was selected.
He brought the tribe of Judah forward clan by clan, and the clan of Zerah was selected. He brought the clan of Zerah forward household by household, and Zabdi was selected.
He brought his household forward man by man, and Achar son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, from the tribe of Judah, was selected.
Joshua said to Achar, “Give glory to the Lord, the God of Israel, and give him praise. Tell me what you have done, and do not hide it from me.”
Achar answered Joshua, “Truly, I have sinned against the Lord, the God of Israel. This is what I did:

“I saw among the plunder a Babylonian robe, which was beautiful, two hundred shekels of silver, and a bar of gold weighing fifty shekels. I coveted them and took them. Look, I have them buried in the ground inside my tent, with the silver underneath.”
Joshua sent men, and they ran to his tent. They saw that the things were buried in his tent, with the silver underneath.
They took them from his tent and brought them to Joshua and to all Israel, and he laid them before the Lord.

Joshua took Achar son of Zerah, along with the silver, the robe, and the gold bar. He also took his sons, his daughters, his cattle, his donkeys, his sheep, his tent, and everything he had, with all Israel accompanying him, and brought them up to the Valley of Achor.
Joshua said to him, “Why have you brought trouble on us? May the Lord bring trouble on you today.” All Israel stoned him and everything he had, and burned them with fire.
They raised a heap of large stones over him, which remains to this day. Then the Lord turned from his fierce anger. That is why that place is called the Valley of Achor to this day.

The Lord said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid or dismayed. Take all the people with you and wage war. Get up and go up to Ai, because I have delivered the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land into your hands.
Do to Ai and its king as you did to Jericho and its king. But you may take its plunder and livestock for yourselves. Set an ambush behind the city.”
Joshua and all the fighting men got up to go up to Ai. Joshua chose three thousand men, mighty in strength, and sent them out at night.
He commanded them, saying, “See that when you lie in ambush against the city, behind it, you do not go too far from the city. All of you must be ready.
I and the people with me will approach the city. When they come out to meet us as before, we will flee from them.
They will come out after us and pursue us away from the city, because they will say, ‘They are fleeing from us as before.’ And we will flee from them.
Then you must rise from your ambush and destroy the city. The Lord your God will deliver it into your hands.
When you have captured the city, burn it with fire. Do as the Lord has said. See, I have given you your orders.”
Joshua sent them out, and they went to the place of ambush. They took up their position between Bethel and Ai, west of the city. Joshua spent that night among the people.
Joshua rose early in the morning and counted the people. He and the elders of Israel went up to Ai ahead of the people.
All the fighting men with him went up and approached the city opposite them. They camped north of Ai, with a ravine between them and Ai.
Joshua took five thousand men and stationed them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, west of the city.
He positioned his people and his entire camp north of the city, with the rear guard west of the city. That night Joshua went among the people.

When the king of Ai saw this, he hurried, and the men of the city rose and went out to meet Israel. All the people of Ai were in the plain, but the people did not know that an ambush had been set against them behind the city.
Joshua and all Israel scattered before them, fleeing along the road to the wilderness.
All the people of Ai raised a shout to pursue them. They pursued Joshua and emptied the city.
Not a man remained in Ai or Bethel who did not go out after Israel. They left the city open and pursued Israel.
The Lord said to Joshua, “Raise the spear in your hand toward Ai, because I have delivered it into your hands.” So Joshua raised the spear he was holding in his hand toward the city.
The men lying in ambush quickly rose from their position and ran swiftly as soon as he moved his hand. They entered the city, captured it, and hurried to set the city on fire.

The men of Ai turned around and saw the smoke of their city rising to the sky. They could not escape in any direction, and the people of Israel who had been fleeing into the wilderness turned against their pursuers.
Joshua and all Israel saw that the men lying in ambush had captured the city and that smoke was rising from the city. They turned back and struck down the men of Ai.

The others came out of the city to meet them, so the men of Ai were caught in the middle of Israel, with one group on one side and the other group on the other. They struck them down and left no survivor.
They captured the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.

When Israel had finished killing all the inhabitants of Ai in the fields and in the wilderness where they had pursued them, and all of them had fallen by the sword until they were completely destroyed, all Israel returned to Ai and struck it down with the sword.
All who fell that day, both men and women, numbered twelve thousand—all the people of Ai.
Joshua did not lower the hand with which he had raised the spear until he had destroyed all the inhabitants of Ai.
The Israelites took only the livestock and the plunder of that city for themselves, according to the word of the Lord, which he had commanded Joshua.
Joshua burned Ai and made it a permanently ruined mound, as it remains to this day.

He hung the king of Ai on a tree until evening. When the sun set, Joshua gave orders, and they took the body down from the tree and threw it at the entrance to the city gate. They raised a heap of large stones over him, which remains to this day.
Then Joshua built an altar to the LORD, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal.

As Moses, the servant of the Lord, had commanded the Israelites, as it is written in the book of the law of Moses: an altar of whole stones that no iron tool had touched. On it they offered whole burnt offerings to the Lord and sacrificed sacrifices.
There, on these stones of the altar, he wrote a copy of the law of Moses, which he wrote in the presence of the Israelites.

All Israel, with its elders, scribes, and judges, stood on both sides of the ark, facing the priests and Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord. Half of them faced Mount Gerizim, and half faced Mount Ebal, as Moses, the servant of the Lord, had previously commanded for the blessing of Israel.
Afterward Joshua read all the words of the law, the blessings and the curses, everything written in the book of the law.
Joshua did not leave unread a single word of all that Moses had commanded. He read it before the whole assembly of Israel, before the women, the children, and the foreigners living among them.

When all the kings beyond the Jordan, in the mountains, in the valleys, and along all the shores of the Great Sea facing Lebanon—the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—heard,
they gathered together with one accord to wage war against Joshua and Israel.
The inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Ai and Jericho.
They too acted cunningly. They went and supplied themselves with provisions, putting worn-out sacks on their donkeys and worn-out wineskins that were torn and tied up.
They wore worn-out, patched sandals on their feet and worn-out clothes, and the bread they carried as provisions had dried out and become moldy.
They came to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal and said to him and to the people of Israel, “We have come from a distant country. Now make a treaty with us.”
The Israelites said to the Hivites, “If you live among us, why should you receive a pledge from us?”
They said to Joshua, “We are your servants.” Joshua said to them, “Where are you from, and where have you come from?”
They said to him, “Your servants have come from a land and a country very far away because of the name of the Lord your God, for we have heard of his fame and everything he did in Egypt,
and everything he did to the two kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan—to Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth.
Our elders and all the inhabitants of our land told us, ‘Take provisions with you for the journey, go to meet them, and say to them, “We are your servants. Now make a treaty with us.”’
They said to Joshua, “This bread of ours was still warm when we took it from our homes as provisions on the day we set out to come to you. But now look: it has dried out and become moldy.

These wineskins were new when we filled them, but look: they have split open. These clothes and sandals of ours were new when we took them with us, but look: they have worn out, because the journey was so very long.”
The men took these provisions of theirs and went away, but they did not ask the LORD for guidance.
Joshua made peace with them and gave them his pledge to spare their lives, and the leaders of the assembly swore an oath to them.
Three days after he had given them his pledge, they heard that these people were their neighbors and lived among them.
The Israelites set out and reached their towns on the third day. The names of their towns were Gibeon, Chephirah, Iroth, and Kiriath-nearim.
The Israelites did not kill them, because the leaders of the assembly had sworn an oath to them by the Lord, the God of Israel. The whole assembly grumbled and argued against the leaders.
The leaders of the assembly said, “We have sworn an oath to them by the Lord, the God of Israel. Now we cannot harm them.
This is what we will do: we will let them live, so that wrath does not come upon us because of the oaths we swore to them.”

The leaders said to the Israelites, “Let them live and become wood gatherers and water carriers for the whole assembly.” So they became wood gatherers and water carriers for the whole assembly, just as the leaders had told them.
Joshua summoned them and said to them, “Why did you deceive us and tell us, ‘We live very far from you,’ when you actually live beside us?
Now you are cursed, and there will always be men from among you gathering wood and carrying water for the house of God.”

They answered Joshua, “Your servants were clearly told what the Lord your God commanded his servant Moses: to give you the whole land and to destroy all the inhabitants of the land before you. We feared greatly for our lives, and we did this.
Now, here we are in your hands. Do to us whatever seems good to you.”
He did this for them: he rescued them from the hands of Israel and did not kill them.
That very day Joshua made them wood gatherers and water carriers for the assembly and for the altar of the Lord, to this day, in the place the Lord chose.

When Adoni-zedek, king of Jerusalem, heard that Joshua had captured Ai and destroyed it, doing to Ai and its king just as he had done to Jericho and its king, and that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were living among them,
they were very afraid, because Gibeon was a large city, like one of the royal cities. It was larger than Ai, and all its men were mighty warriors.
Adoni-zedek, king of Jerusalem, sent messengers to Hoham, king of Hebron, to Baran, king of Jarmuth, to Naphia, king of Lachish, and to Debir, king of Eglon, with this message:
“Come up to me and help me, and let us fight against Gibeon, because it has made peace with Joshua and Israel.”

The five kings of the Amorites—the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon—gathered and went up with all their armies. They camped against Gibeon and waged war against it.

The men of Gibeon sent messengers to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal and said to him, “Do not abandon your servants, for all the kings of the Amorites who live in the hill country have gathered against us.”
Joshua went up from Gilgal, with all the fighting men who were with him and all the mighty warriors.
The Lord said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them, because I have handed them over to you. Not one of them can stand against you.”
Joshua came upon them suddenly, having marched up from Gilgal all night.

The Lord threw them into confusion before Israel, and the Israelites inflicted a great defeat on them at Gibeon of Beth-horon. They pursued them along the road up to Beth-horon and struck them down as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

As they fled from Israel and were going down the descent of Beth-horon, the Lord hurled large stones from heaven upon them as far as Azekah, and they died. More died from the hailstones than the Israelites killed with the sword.

Then Joshua spoke before the Lord on the day when the Lord handed the Amorites over to Israel. Joshua said in the presence of the Israelites, “Sun, remain over Gibeon, and you, moon, over the valley of Aijalon.”

The sun remained, and the moon stood still, until the people had taken vengeance on their enemies. This is written in the Book of Praises. The sun stood still in the middle of the sky and did not hurry to set, for about a whole day.
There was no day like that one, before it or after it, when the Lord listened to Joshua's voice in this way, because the Lord was fighting for Israel.
Joshua and all Israel with him returned to the camp at Gilgal.
These five kings fled and hid in the cave at Makkedah.
Joshua received word, and they told him, “These five kings have been found hiding in the cave at Makkedah.”
Joshua said, “Roll large stones and place them against the entrance of the cave, and leave men there to guard them.
But you must not stop. Pursue your enemies and overtake them. Do not let them enter the city, because the Lord your God has handed them over to you.”

When Joshua and the Israelites had finished slaughtering them in a great slaughter, until they were completely destroyed and not one survivor remained, they brought those rebels of Gibeon into their fortified city.
Then all the people returned safely to Joshua at the camp at Makkedah. No one uttered a word against anyone of the house of Israel.
Joshua said, “Open the entrance of the cave and bring these five kings out of the cave to me.”
They did as Joshua told them and brought the five kings out of the cave to him: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon.

When they brought these kings out to Joshua, Joshua summoned all the military commanders who were accompanying him and said to them, “Come forward and put your feet on the necks of these kings.” They came forward and put their feet on the necks of these kings.
Joshua said to them, “Do not be afraid or dismayed. Be strong and courageous, because this is what the Lord will do to all your enemies against whom you fight.”
After that, Joshua killed them and hung them on five trees. They remained hanging on the trees until evening.

At sunset Joshua gave the order, and they took the hanging men down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had been hiding. They placed large stones over the entrance of the cave, which remain to this day.

Joshua captured Makkedah that day and struck it with the sword. He killed its king and everyone in it, leaving none of them alive. He did to the king of Makkedah what he had done to the king of Jericho.
Joshua, with all Israel accompanying him, went from [?] to Libnah and fought against Libnah.

The Lord also delivered it into Israel’s hands. They struck it and its king with the sword, along with everyone in it. He left no survivor there, and Joshua did to its king what he had done to the king of Jericho.
Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Libnah to Lachish, camped against it, and fought against it.
The Lord delivered Lachish into Israel’s hands. He captured it on the second day and struck it and everyone in it with the sword, just as he had done to Libnah.
Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish. Joshua struck him and his people with the sword as well, leaving him no survivor.
Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Lachish to Eglon, camped against it, and fought against it.
He captured it that day and struck it and everyone in it with the sword, just as he had done to Lachish.
Joshua and all Israel with him went up from Eglon to Hebron and fought against it.

He captured it and struck it with the sword, along with its king, all its towns, and everyone in it. He left none of them alive, just as he had done to Eglon and everyone in it, whom he had destroyed.
Joshua and all Israel with him turned back toward Debir and fought against it.

He captured it, its king, and all its towns, and struck them with the sword. He destroyed everyone in it and left none of them alive. He did to Debir and its king just as he had done to Hebron, and just as he had done to Libnah and its king.

Joshua devastated the whole land—the hill country, the south, the plain, and Ashdod—and all their kings. He left none of them alive and destroyed all their forces, just as the Lord, the God of Israel, had commanded him.
Joshua destroyed them from Rekem-Gaya to Gaza, including the whole land of Goshen, as far as Gibeon.
Joshua conquered all these kings and their territories in a single campaign, because the Lord, the God of Israel, was with him, and he was fighting for Israel.
When Nabin king of Hazor heard, he sent word to Jobab king of Merom, to the king of Shimron, and to the king of Achshaph,
and to the kings north of him, in the hill country, in the south, in the plain of Chinnereth and its plains, and in Naphath-dor to the west,
and to the Canaanites in the east and west, the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, and Jebusites in the hill country, and the Hivites below Mount Hermon in the land of the watchtowers.
They came out with all their armies, as numerous as the sand on the seashore, with a very great number of horses and chariots.
All these kings assembled and camped together by the waters of Merom, and prepared to fight against Israel.
The Lord said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them, because tomorrow at this time I will have them all lying slain before the Israelites. Destroy their horses and burn their chariots with fire.”
Joshua came suddenly to the waters of Merom, with all the fighting men who were with him, and they attacked them.

The Lord delivered them into Israel’s hands. They struck them down and pursued them as far as Great Sidon, as far as the gathering place of the waters, and as far as the valley of Mizpah to the east. They struck them down, and he left none of them alive.
Joshua did to them as the Lord had told him: he destroyed their horses and burned their chariots with fire.
At that time Joshua turned back and captured Hazor, and killed its king with the sword, because Hazor had formerly been the head of these kingdoms.
He killed everyone in it with the sword, leaving no one alive, and burned Hazor with fire.
Joshua captured all the cities of these kings and their kings, and killed them with the sword, just as Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded him.
Israel burned all the towns standing on hills, and Joshua burned Hazor.
The Israelites took all the plunder of these cities and the livestock for themselves. But they killed all the people with the sword until they had destroyed them completely, leaving no one alive.
Just as the Lord had commanded his servant Moses, so Moses commanded Joshua, and so Joshua did. He left nothing undone of all that the Lord had commanded Moses.
Joshua took all this mountainous land, all the south, all the land of the plain, and all the mountains and their valleys.
From the mountain that divides and rises toward Seir as far as Gadgad in the valley of Lebanon below Mount Hermon, Joshua captured all their kings and killed them.
Joshua waged war against all these kings for many days.

Not a town remained that was not handed over to the Israelites and destroyed by them, except the Hivites living in Gibeon, whom Joshua kept alive. Joshua spared them to serve Israel. Joshua captured all these kingdoms and destroyed them.

For it was the Lord's doing that their hearts became bold enough to go out to war against Israel, so that they would be destroyed and receive no mercy, but be wiped out, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.

At that time Joshua came and destroyed the giants in the hill country, from Hebron, Debir, and Gebal, and from all the hill country of Judah and all the hill country of Israel. Joshua destroyed them along with their cities.
Not a man remained in the land of the Israelites, except those who remained in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
Joshua took the whole land, just as the Lord had told Moses, and Joshua gave it to Israel as an inheritance, divided among their tribes. Then the land rested from war.

These are the kings of the land whom the Israelites killed and whose territories they took possession of beyond the Jordan to the east, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon, including the whole eastern plain:

Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon and ruled from Aroer on the bank of the Arnon Valley, including the middle of the valley and half of Gilead, as far as the Aphek stream at the border of the Ammonites;
and the plain as far as the Sea of Chinnereth on the east, and as far as the Sea of the Plain, the Salt Sea, east of the road to Beth-ashimon, and southward below Ashdoth-ramah.
and the territory of Og king of Bashan, of the family of the giants, who lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
He ruled over Mount Ashimon, Salecah, and all Bashan as far as the border of Endor and Maacath, and over half of Gilead and the territory of Sihon king of Heshbon.
Moses, the servant of the LORD, killed him and gave it as an inheritance to Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

These are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the Israelites killed beyond the Jordan to the west, from Gilgal in the valley of Lebanon to the mountain that divides and rises toward Seir. Joshua gave the land to the tribes of Israel as an inheritance according to their allotted portions:
in the mountains, the valleys, the Arabah, Ashdod, the wilderness, and the south—the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
These are the kings of the land whom Joshua killed: the king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel, one.
One king of Jerusalem; one king of Hebron.
the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;
the king of Debir, one; the king of Hormah, one;
the king of Geder, one; the king of Eder, one;
the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam [?], one;
the king of Maqar, one; the king of Bethel, one;
the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;
the king of Aphek, one; the king of Nashron, one;
the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;
One king of Shimron and Meron; one king of Achshaph.
One king of Taanach; one king of Megiddo.
One king of Rekem; one king of Nekmeam and Carmel.
One king of Dor and Naphath-dor; one king of the valley and Gilgal.
One king of Tirzah. All the kings whom Joshua destroyed numbered thirty-one.
Joshua was old and advanced in years, and the Lord said to him, “Look, you are old and advanced in years, and a very great amount of land still remains to be taken possession of.
This is the land that remains: all the region of the Philistines and all the territory of Endor,

From Shihor, which is east of Egypt, to the northern border of Ekron, it is counted as Canaanite territory: the five rulers of the Philistines—the Gazites, Ashdodites, Ashkelonites, Gittites, and Ekronites—and the Avvites
to the south; all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah belonging to the Sidonians, as far as Aphek and as far as the border of the Amorites;
the land of Gebal and all Lebanon toward the sunrise, in Gilead below Mount Hermon, as far as the entrance to Hamath.

All the inhabitants of the mountains as far as the region of the hot springs, and all the Sidonians—I, the Lord, will destroy them before the Israelites. Only [?] the land of Israel, just as I commanded you.
Divide this land into inheritances for the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh with them.
For Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh received their inheritance, which Moses gave them beyond the Jordan to the east, just as my servant Moses gave it to them:
from Aroer on the bank of the Arnon Valley, including the town in the middle of the valley, and all the plain to the west as far as Ribon;
all the towns of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the boundary of the Ammonites;
Gilead, the territory of Endor and Kuros, all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah;
all the kingdom of Og in Mathnin, who reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei. He remained from the remnant of the giants whom Moses killed, and they took possession of their land.
The Israelites did not destroy the peoples of Endor and Cyrrhus, and the people of Endor and Cyrrhus have lived among the Israelites to this day.
Only to the tribe of Levi did he give no share, because the offerings of the Lord, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, as Moses told them.
Moses gave an inheritance to the tribe of Reuben according to their clans.
Their territory extended from Aroer, beside the bank of the Arnon Valley, including the town in the valley and the whole plain as far as Riba.
Heshbon and all the towns in the plain, Ribon, Matbaal, and Beth-bene-ammon;
Jahaz, Karmoth, and Anath;
Kiriathaim, Shemama, Jezereth, and Seir, which is on the mountain in the valley;
Beth-peor, Ashtaroth, Pisgah, and Beth-jeshimoth.

It included all the towns in the plain and the entire kingdom of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon. Moses and the Israelites killed him in Midian, along with his leaders—Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba—these five governors of Sihon who lived in the land.
The Israelites also killed Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, with the sword, along with those they killed.
The boundary of the Reubenites was the Jordan. This was the inheritance of the Reubenites according to their clans: the towns and their surrounding lands.
Moses gave an inheritance to the tribe of Gad, to the descendants of Gad according to their clans.
Their territory included Jazer and all the towns of Gilead, half the land of the Ammonites, as far as Aroer, which is opposite Rabbah.
It extended from Heshbon to Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the boundary of Debir.

In the valley it included Beth-athim, Beth-nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, and the rest of the kingdom of Sihon, king of Heshbon. Their boundaries extended to the Jordan and to the end of the Sea of Chinnereth, on the eastern side of the Jordan.
This was the inheritance of the descendants of Gad according to their clans: the towns and their surrounding lands.
Moses gave an inheritance to the half-tribe of Manasseh, and it became the portion of the descendants of Manasseh according to their clans.
Their territory extended from Mahanaim and included all Bashan, the entire kingdom of Og, king of Bashan, and all the villages of Jair in Bashan—sixty towns.

Half of Gilead, together with Ashtaroth and Edrei, the towns of Og's kingdom in Bashan—these towns and their villages Moses gave to the descendants of Machir son of Manasseh, to half the descendants of Machir according to their clans.
Moses gave these two tribes and the half-tribe their inheritance in the plain of Moab, on the eastern side of the Jordan.
Moses gave no inheritance to the tribe of Levi, because the Lord, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as he told them.

These are the lands the Israelites inherited in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral families of the tribes of Israel gave them as their inheritance.
Their inheritance was allotted as the Lord had commanded through Moses, to be given to the nine tribes and the half-tribe.
For Moses had given an inheritance to the two tribes and the half-tribe beyond the Jordan, but he gave the Levites no inheritance among them.
For the descendants of Joseph formed two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. He gave the Levites no share in the land except towns to live in and surrounding lands for their livestock and possessions.
The Israelites did as the Lord had commanded Moses, and they divided the land.
The people of Judah approached Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to Joshua, “You know what the Lord said to Moses his servant about you and me at Kadesh-barnea.
I was forty years old when Moses, the servant of God, sent me from Kadesh-barnea to explore the land, and I brought him back a report according to what was in my heart.
Our brothers who went up with us frightened the people, but I followed the LORD my God wholeheartedly.
Moses swore at that time, saying, ‘The land on which your foot has walked will be an inheritance for you and your children forever, because you have followed the Lord God wholeheartedly.’

And now, look, the Lord has given us rest, as he said. It has been forty-five years since the Lord spoke this word to Moses, for him to lead Israel through the wilderness. Today I am eighty-five years old.
Even now I am as strong as I was on the day Moses sent me. My strength then and now is the same, for battle and for going out and coming in.

Now give me this hill country that the Lord spoke of on that day. You yourself heard on that day that giants were there and that the cities were large and fortified. Perhaps the Lord will be with me, and I will destroy them, as the Lord said.”
Joshua blessed Caleb son of Jephunneh and gave him the fortified city of Hebron as an inheritance.
For this reason the fortified city of Hebron has been the inheritance of Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite to this day, because he followed the Lord, the God of Israel, wholeheartedly.
The fortified city of Hebron was formerly called Kiriath-arba, belonging to the giants. And the land rested from war.
The allotment of the tribe of Judah, according to their clans, lay along the border of Edom, extending to the wilderness of Zin and to the farthest southern edge.
Their boundary ran from the southern end of the Salt Sea and went up from there to the tongue of the sea that faces south.
It goes out from the south to the ascent of Akrabbim, passes to Zin, goes up from the south to Rekem-gai, passes to Hezron, goes up to Addar, and turns toward Karka.
It passes to Azmon and goes out to the stream of Egypt, and the boundary ends in the west. This shall be your southern boundary.
The eastern boundary is the end of the Salt Sea, as far as the end of the Jordan. The boundary on the northern side begins at the tongue of the sea, at the end of the Jordan.
The boundary went up to Laban of the Reubenites.

The boundary goes up to Debir from the Valley of Achor, then turns north toward Gelilah, opposite the ascent of Ramin, south of the stream. The boundary passes by the spring of Shemesh and ends at the spring of Dogel.

The boundary goes up to the Valley of Ben-hinnom, to the southern side of the Jebusites—that is, Jerusalem. The boundary goes up to the summit of the mountain west of the Valley of Ben-hinnom, at the end of the Valley of the Giants.
The boundary turns from the summit of the mountain to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah and goes out to the peak of Mount Ephron. The boundary turns toward Baalah, which is Kiriath-nearim.
The boundary turns west from Baalah toward Mount Seir, passes along the northern side of Mount Jearim, which is Chesalon, goes down to Beth-shemesh, and passes to Timnah.
The boundary goes out to the northern side of Ekron. The boundary turns toward Shikkeron, passes by Mount Baalah, and goes out to Jabneel, and the boundary ends in the west.
Its western boundary is at [?], with its borders. This is the boundary surrounding the descendants of Judah according to their clans.

Joshua gave Caleb son of Jephunneh a share among the descendants of Judah, according to the command of the LORD. Caleb said to Joshua, “Give me this Kiriath-arba, belonging to the father of the giants.” Joshua gave Caleb Kiriath-arba, belonging to the father of the giants, which is Hebron.
There Caleb wiped out the three sons of the giants: Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, sons of the giants.
From there he went up against the inhabitants of Debir. Debir was formerly called Kiriath-sepher.
Caleb said, “Whoever conquers Kiriath-sepher and destroys it, I will give him my daughter Achsah as his wife.”
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s brother, conquered it, and Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah as his wife.
When she became his wife, she desired to ask her father for a field as an inheritance. She lowered herself from the donkey, and Caleb said to her, “What is the matter, my daughter?”
She said to him, “Give me a blessing. Since you have given me land in the south, give me this water basin.” Caleb gave her the upper basin and the lower basin.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of Judah according to their clans.
The towns of the tribe of the descendants of Judah were along the border of Edom in the south. These are the names of the towns of the descendants of Judah: Kabzeel, Eder, and Jagur.
Kinah, Jarmonah, and Gadgada;
Kedesh, Hazor, and Nathnin;
Zib, Atlam, and Bealoth;
Hazor, Hadattah, and Kiriath-hezron.
And Amam, Shema, and Moladah;
and Hazar-addah, Heshmon, and Beth-pelet;
and Hazar-shual, Beersheba, and Biriothna;
and Baal, Alin, and Ezem;
and Eltelam, Achsin, and Hormah;
and Ziklag, Marmannah, and Samsallah;
and Lebaoth, Shiloah, and Irmon—all the towns numbered thirty-six, with their villages.
In the lowland: Eshtaol, Zorah, and Ashnah;
and Hoh, En-gahom, Pattuh, and Elam;
and Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, and Azekah;
and Shaathin, Azithim, Gathar, and Gathronin—fifteen towns with their villages.
And Zenan, Hadashah, and Migdal-gad;
and Dilean, Mizpeh, and Joktheel;
and Lachish, Azkath, and Eglon;
and Cabbon, Lahmas, and Chitlish;
And Adaroth, Beth-dagon, Naamah, and Naqda: sixteen towns with their surrounding lands.
and Libnah, Ether, and Iphtah;
and Ashan, Ashiah, and Ziklag;
and Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah—nine towns with their villages.
And Ekron, its dependent towns, and its villages;
from the west, and the whole territory of Ashdod, with their villages;
Ashdod with its villages and surrounding fields, and Gaza with its villages and surrounding fields, as far as the stream of Egypt, with the Great Sea as the boundary.
And these were in the hill country: Shamir, Jattir, and Socoh;
and Rannah, and Kiriath-sepher, which is Debir;
and Anab, Eshtemoh, and Anim;
and Goshen, Holon, and Giloh—eleven towns with their villages.
And Rib, Rumah, and Ashan;
and Jilum, Beth-tappuah, and Aphek;
and Humtah, Kiriath-arba, which is Hebron, and Zibeon—nine towns with their villages.
And Maon, Carmel, Zib, and Atna;
and Jezreel, Nekmaam, and Zaluah;
and Cain, Gibeah, and Tekna—ten towns with their villages.
And Halhul, Beth-zado, and Gathar;
and Maarath, Beth-anath, and Eltekon—six towns with their villages.
And Rabbath and Kiriath-baal, which is Kiriath-naarin—two towns with their villages.
In the wilderness: Beth-arabah, Middin, and Secacah;
and Jeshan, Ir-mahal, and En-gedi—six towns with their villages.
The descendants of Judah did not destroy the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem. The Jebusites lived with the descendants of Judah in Jerusalem to this day.
The allotment of the descendants of Joseph extended from the Jordan at Jericho to the waters of Jericho, east of the wilderness that goes up from Jericho as far as the hill country of Bethel.
It went from Bethel to Luz and passed into the territory of Eber and Ataroth.
It goes down westward to the territory of Pelat, as far as the territory of Lower Beth-horon and as far as Geder, and it ended in the west.
The descendants of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, received their inheritance.
This was the boundary of the descendants of Ephraim according to their clans: the boundary of their inheritance ran from Ataroth-addar as far as Upper Beth-horon.
The boundary goes out westward along the northern portion. The boundary turns eastward below Shiloh and passes east of Janoah.
It descended from Jaluah to Ataroth, Igrath, Pagar, and Jericho.

It goes out from Tappuah to the Jordan and runs to the western boundary of the stream of Qeba, and it ends in the west. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Ephraim according to their clans.
There were towns set apart for the descendants of Ephraim within the inheritance of the descendants of Manasseh—all these towns and their surrounding fields.
They did not destroy the Canaanites who lived in Geder. The Canaanites lived among Ephraim to this day and were subjected to tribute.

Gilead became the allotment of the tribe of Manasseh, because he was Joseph’s firstborn, and of Machir, Manasseh’s firstborn, the father of Gilead. Because he was the firstborn and a warrior, Gilead and Bashan became his.

There was also an allotment for the remaining descendants of Manasseh according to their clans: for the descendants of Abiezer, the descendants of Helek, the descendants of Nashrael, the descendants of Shuppim, the descendants of Hepher, and the descendants of Shemida. These were the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph according to their clans.
Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, had no sons, only daughters. These are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

They came before Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders of Israel and said, “The Lord commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers, and he gave us one among our father’s brothers according to the Lord’s command. Now give us an inheritance among our fathers’ brothers.” So Joshua gave them an inheritance and a share among their father’s brothers.
Ten portions fell to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan beyond the Jordan.
For the daughters of Manasseh inherited an inheritance along with their brothers, and the land of Gilead belonged to the remaining sons of Manasseh.
The boundary of the descendants of Manasseh ran from the boundary of Maacath, which is to the right of the inhabitants of En-tappuah.
Their land was in Tappuah and [?], and it formed a boundary for the descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph and for the descendants of Ephraim.
Their boundary went down to the stream of the sea, south of the stream by these towns of Ephraim among the towns of Manasseh. Manasseh’s boundary was north of the stream, and it ended in the west.
The south belonged to Ephraim and the north to Manasseh, and the sea was their boundary. They bordered Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.
Opposite Issachar, Manasseh had Beth-shean and its villages, Ibleam and its villages, En-dor and its villages, Taanach and its villages, and Megiddo and its villages: three districts.
The Israelites did not destroy these towns, because the Canaanites were content to live in these towns.
When the Israelites grew strong, they subjected the Canaanites to tribute, but they did not destroy them.
The descendants of Joseph said to Joshua, “Why have you given us only one portion and one tract as an inheritance, when we are a numerous people, since the Lord has blessed us up to this point?”

Joshua said to them, “If you are a numerous people, go up to the woodland on the mountain and clear land for yourselves there in the land of the Perizzites and the giants, since the hill country of Ephraim is too cramped for you.”

The descendants of Joseph said, “The hill country and the towns of the Perizzites are not enough for us, because the Canaanites live in the valley land, in Beth-shean and its villages, and in the Valley of Jezreel.”
Joshua said to the household of Joseph, to the descendants of Ephraim and Manasseh, “You are a numerous people, and you have great strength. Is one portion not enough for you?

Clear the hill country for yourselves, and it will be enough for you. The slopes of the hill country will be yours as far as its outer limits. Destroy the Canaanites and the Perizzites, even though they have large, strong iron chariots and are powerful.”
The whole congregation of the Israelites assembled at Shiloh and set up the tent of meeting there. The land had been subdued before them.
There remained seven tribes among the Israelites whose inheritance had not been divided among them.
Joshua said to the Israelites, “How long will you delay going in to take possession of the land that the Lord, the God of your ancestors, has given you?
Choose three men from each tribe, and I will send them out. They will set out, travel through the land, and describe it in writing according to their inheritance. Then they will come to me.
They will divide the land into seven portions. Judah will remain within its territory in the south, and the household of Joseph will remain within their territory in the north.
You are to describe the land in writing in seven portions and bring the description here to me. I will show you the portion chosen before the Lord our God.

For the Levites have no share among you, because the priesthood of the Lord is their inheritance. Gad, Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance beyond the Jordan to the east, which Moses, the servant of the Lord, gave them.”

The men set out and went. Joshua instructed those who went to describe the land in writing, saying to them, “Go, travel through the land and describe it in writing. Then return here to me, and I will cast lots for your portions before the Lord at Shiloh.”
The men went and traveled through the land. They recorded the towns in seven portions on a scroll and came to Joshua at the city of Shiloh.
They cast lots for them at Shiloh before the Lord, and there Joshua divided the land into shares for the Israelites.
The lot for the tribe of Benjamin came up according to their clans. The territory of their inheritance lay between the descendants of Judah and the descendants of Joseph.
Their boundary on the north began at the Jordan. The boundary went up along the northern side of Jericho, went up through the hill country westward, and ended at the wilderness of Beth-aven.
From there the boundary passed to Luz, along the southern side of Luz, which is Bethel. The boundary went down to Ataroth-addar, on the mountain south of Lower Beth-horon.

The boundary turned along the western side toward the south, from the mountain facing Beth-horon on the south, and ended at Kiriath-baal, which is Kiriath-jearim, a city of the descendants of Judah. This was the western side.
The southern side began at the edge of Kiriath-jearim. The boundary went out toward the sea and continued to the spring of the waters of Naphtali.

The boundary descended to the end of the mountain facing the valley of Ben-hinnom, which lies north of the Valley of the Giants. The boundary descended through Ben-hinnom, along the southern side of the Jebusites, and went down to En-dogel.
It turned northward and went out to En-shemesh, then went out to Geliloth, opposite the ascent of Ramin, and descended to Laban and to Bohan son of Reuben.
It passes along the side facing the valley to the north and descends into the valley.
The boundary passed along the northern side of Beth-hoglah. The boundary ended at the northern tongue of the Salt Sea and at the southern banks of the Jordan. This was the southern boundary.
The Jordan formed the boundary on the eastern side. This was the inheritance of the descendants of Benjamin, according to their clans, with its surrounding boundaries.
The towns of the tribe of the descendants of Benjamin, according to their clans, were Jericho, Zebith, Hoglah, Emek, and Keziz.
Beth-arabah, Zemaraim, and Bethel;
Avvim, Parah, and Ophrah;
Kephar-umqa, Ophli, and Geba: fourteen towns with their villages.
Gibeon, Ramah, and Beru;
Mizpah, Chephirah, and Mozah;
Rekem, Raphael, and Taralah;
Zela, Gebirah, Jebus—which is Jerusalem—Gibeath, and Kiriathaim: fourteen towns with their villages. This was the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Benjamin, according to their clans.
The second lot came out for the tribe of the descendants of Simeon, according to their clans. Their inheritance was within the inheritance of the descendants of Judah.
They had in their inheritance Beersheba, Sheba, and Moladah.
Hazar-shual, Balah, and Ezem;
Eltolad, Bethel, and Hormah;
Ziklag, Beth-marcaboth, and Hazar-susah;
Beth-lebaoth and Sharuhen: fourteen towns with their villages.
Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan: four towns with their villages;
Also included were all the villages surrounding these towns, as far as Baath Beth-ramah in the south. This was the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Simeon, according to their clans.

The inheritance of the descendants of Simeon came from the territory of the descendants of Judah, because the portion of the descendants of Judah was too large. So the descendants of Simeon received an inheritance from their inheritance.
The third lot came up for the descendants of Zebulun, according to their clans. The boundary of their inheritance extended as far as Ashdod.
Their boundary went up westward to Ramath-shual, reached Dabbesheth, and reached the valley opposite Nekmaam.
It turned from Ashdod toward the sunrise, to the boundary of Chesulloth and Bathur, went out to Rabbath, and went up to Japhia.
From there it passed eastward to Gath, Hepher, Attah, and Kazin, and went out to Rimmon, Methoah, and Avvah.
The boundary curved around north of Hannathon and ended at the valley of Kaphtanael.
It extended to Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem: twelve towns with their villages.
This was the inheritance of the descendants of Zebulun, according to their clans.
The fourth lot fell to the descendants of Issachar, according to their clans.
Their territory included Jezreel, Chesulloth, and Shuim.
And Hapharaim, Shion, and Ahthar.
And Daberath, Kishion, and Ebez.
And Ramath-en, Enim, En-haddah, and Beth-pazzin.
The boundary reached Tabor, Shahazumah, and Beth-shemesh, and their boundary ended at the Jordan: thirteen towns with their villages.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Issachar according to their clans: the towns with their villages.
The fifth lot fell to the tribe of the descendants of Asher according to their clans.
Their territory included Helkath, Hali, Beten, and Achshaph.
And Allammelech, Amad, and Mishal. It reached Carmel on the west, Shihor, and Lebith.
It turned toward the sunrise to Beth-dagon and reached Zebulun and the valley of Iphtah-el to the north, and Beth, Emek, and Neiel. It went out to Cabul on the north.
And to Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, as far as Great Sidon.
The boundary turned to Ramah and extended as far as Tyre, the fortified city. The boundary turned to Hosah and ended to the west, at the brook of Jarib.
And Umka, Aphek, and Rehob: twenty-two towns with their villages.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Asher according to their clans: these towns with their villages.
The sixth lot fell to the descendants of Naphtali according to their clans.
Their boundary ran from Heleph, Elon, Zaanannim, Admah, Nekeb, and Nebael as far as Lakkum, and ended at the Jordan.
The boundary turned westward to Aznoth-boz and went out from there to Hukkok. It reached Zebulun on the south, Asher on the west, and Judah at the Jordan toward the sunrise.
And among the large cities were Tyre, Sidon, Hammath, Kiriath, and Chinnereth.
And Adamah, Damah, and Hazor.
And Kedesh, Edrei, and En-zur.
And Dion, Migdal-el, Haddum, Beth-anath, and Beth-shemesh: nineteen cities with their villages.
The seventh lot fell to the descendants of Dan according to their clans.
The territory of their inheritance included Zorah, Eshtaol, and the town of Shemesh.
And Shaalabbin, Aijalon, and Nethlah.
And Elon, Timnah, and Ekron.
And Eltekeh, Gibbethon, and Baalath.
And Jehudith, Baal-debak, and Gath-rimmon.
And Me Jarkon and Karkon, as far as the boundary opposite Elath.

The territory of the descendants of Dan slipped from their possession. The descendants of Dan went up and fought against the people of Aino. They captured it, struck it with the edge of the sword, took possession of it, and settled in it. They named Aino Dan, after their ancestor Dan.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Dan, according to their clans: these cities, towns, and their villages.
When they had finished taking possession of the land within its boundaries, the Israelites gave Joshua son of Nun an inheritance among them.
At the LORD's command, they gave him the town he requested, Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim. He built up the town and settled in it.

These were the inheritances that Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral families of the tribes of Israel assigned by lot at Shiloh, before the LORD, at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. So they finished dividing the land.
The LORD said to Joshua:
Tell the Israelites: Set aside towns of refuge for yourselves, as I told you through my servant Moses.
A killer who kills someone accidentally and unknowingly may flee there. They will be a refuge for you from the avenger of blood.

He must flee to one of these towns, stand at the entrance to the town gate, and speak before the elders of that town, presenting his case. They must take him into the town with them and give him a place to live among them.
When the avenger of blood pursues him, they must not hand the killer over to him, because he struck his neighbor unintentionally and had not hated him previously.

He must live in that town until he stands before the assembly for judgment, until the death of the high priest serving in those days. Then the killer may return and come to his house, his town, and the city from which he fled.

Then they set apart these towns as places of refuge: Rekem in Galilee, in the hill country of Naphtali; Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim; and Kiriath-arba, which is Hebron, in the hill country of Judah.

Across the Jordan, east of Jericho, they designated Bezer in the wilderness, situated on the plain, from the tribe of Reuben; Ramoth-gilead from the tribe of Gad; and Golan in Bashan from the tribe of Manasseh.

These are the towns of deliverance and refuge for all the Israelites and for the foreigners living among them, so that anyone who kills someone unintentionally may flee there and not be handed over to the avenger of blood before standing before the assembly for judgment.
The heads of the priests and Levites approached Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral families of the tribes of Israel.
They said to them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, “The Lord commanded through Moses that you give us towns to live in, with their pasturelands for our livestock.”
So the Israelites gave the Levites these towns and their pasturelands out of their inheritance, according to the Lord’s command.

The lot fell to the clan of Kohath, to the descendants of Aaron the priest among the Levites. They gave them by lot thirteen towns from the tribe of Judah, the tribe of Simeon, and the tribe of Benjamin.
To the remaining descendants of Kohath they gave ten towns from the tribe of Ephraim, the tribe of Dan, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
To the descendants of Gershon they gave by lot thirteen towns from the tribe of Issachar, the tribe of Asher, the tribe of Naphtali, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
To the descendants of Merari, according to their clans, they gave twelve towns from the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and the tribe of Zebulun.
The Israelites gave the Levites these towns and their pasturelands by lot, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
These are the names of the towns they gave from the tribe of Judah and the tribe of Simeon, listed by name.
They belonged to the descendants of Aaron, of the clan of Kohath, among the descendants of Levi, because the first lot fell to them.
They gave them Kiriath-arba, belonging to the father of the giants, which is Hebron in the hill country of Judah, together with its surrounding pasturelands.
But the fields of the town and the rest of its surrounding lands they gave to Caleb son of Jephunneh as his inheritance.
To the descendants of Aaron the priest they gave Hebron, the city of refuge from the slain [?], with its pasturelands, and Libnah with its pasturelands.
And Jattir with its pasturelands, and Eshtemoa with its pasturelands.
And Holon with its pasturelands, and Debir with its pasturelands.
Ain with its pasturelands, Juttah with its pasturelands, and Beth-shemesh with its pasturelands: nine towns from the tribes of Judah and Simeon.
And from the tribe of Benjamin: Gibeon with its pasturelands, and Geba with its pasturelands.
And Anathoth with its pasturelands, and Almon with its pasturelands: four cities.
All the towns of the descendants of Aaron the priest were thirteen, with their pasturelands.
The clan of the Levites who were the remaining descendants of Kohath received the towns allotted to them from the tribe of Ephraim.
They gave them Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, the city of refuge for killers, with its pasturelands, and Geder with its pasturelands.
And Kibzaim with its pasturelands, and Beth-horon with its pasturelands: four towns with their pasturelands.
And from the tribe of Dan: Eltekeh with its pasturelands, and Gibbethon with its pasturelands.
And Aijalon with its pasturelands, and Gath-rimmon with its pasturelands: four towns with their pasturelands.
From the half-tribe of Manasseh, Taanach with its pasturelands and Gath-rimmon with its pasturelands: two towns with their pasturelands.
In all, ten towns and cities with their pasturelands belonged to the clan of the remaining descendants of Kohath.

The descendants of Gershon, of the clan of the Levites, received their towns from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Golan in Bashan, a city of refuge for killers, with its pasturelands, and Ashtaroth with its pasturelands: two towns with their pasturelands.
And from the tribe of Issachar: Kishion with its pasturelands, and Daberath with its pasturelands.
And Jarmuth with its pasturelands, and En-gad with its pasturelands: four towns with their pasturelands.
And from the tribe of Asher: Mishal with its pasturelands, and Ekron with its pasturelands.
And Helkath with its pasturelands, and Rehob with its pasturelands: four towns with their pasturelands.

From the tribe of Naphtali: Rekem in Galilee, the city of refuge for killers, with its pasturelands, Hamrod with its pasturelands, and Kartan with its pasturelands: three towns with their pasturelands.
All the towns of the clan of the descendants of Gershon were thirteen towns with their pasturelands.
And from the tribe of Zebulun: Nakah with its pasturelands, and Kartan with its pasturelands.
And Rimmon with its pasturelands, and Jahla with its pasturelands: four towns with their pasturelands.
Their towns were from the tribe of Reuben: Jahaz with its pasturelands.
Four towns with their pasturelands.
From the tribe of Gad: Ramoth-gilead, the city of refuge for killers, with its pasturelands, and Mahanaim with its pasturelands.
And Heshbon with its pasturelands, and Jazer with its pasturelands: four towns with their pasturelands.
These were the towns of the descendants of Merari, according to their clans, who remained from the tribe of the Levites. Twelve towns with their pasturelands fell to them by lot.
All these towns of the Levites were within the inheritance of the Israelites. The towns of the Levites numbered forty-eight, with their pasturelands.
These towns and cities were inhabited, each town with its pasturelands surrounding it. All these towns and cities were arranged in this way.
The Lord gave Israel all the land that he had sworn to give their ancestors. They took possession of it and settled in it.
The Lord gave them rest on every side, just as he had sworn to their ancestors. Not one of their enemies could stand against them; the Lord handed all their enemies over to them.
Not one of all the good things that the Lord had spoken to the house of Israel failed; they all came to pass.
Then Joshua summoned the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
He said to them, “You have kept everything that Moses, the Lord’s servant, told you, and you have obeyed me in everything I commanded you.
You have not abandoned your fellow Israelites throughout these many days, right up to today, and you have kept the commandments of the Lord your God.

Now the Lord God has given your fellow Israelites rest, just as he told them. So turn back and go to your towns and to the land of your inheritance, which Moses, the Lord’s servant, gave you beyond the Jordan to the east.

Only be very careful to carry out the commandments and laws that Moses, the Lord’s servant, commanded you: to love the Lord your God, to keep his commandments, to hold fast to him, and to serve him with all your heart and all your soul.”
Joshua blessed them and sent them away, and they went to their towns.

To half the tribe of Manasseh, Moses had given land in Bashan, and to the other half Joshua gave land alongside their fellow Israelites beyond the Jordan to the west. Joshua sent them away, and they went to their towns, and he blessed them.
