He said to them, “Return to your towns and to the land of your inheritance with great wealth and very many livestock, with silver, gold, bronze, iron, and very large quantities of clothing. Share the plunder of your enemies with your fellow Israelites.”

The descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh turned back and departed from the Israelites at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, to go to the land of Gilead, the land of their inheritance, which they had received according to the Lord’s command through Moses.

They came to Gilgal beside the Jordan in the land of Canaan. There the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh built an altar beside the Jordan, an altar impressive in appearance.

The Israelites heard that the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh had built an altar facing the land of Canaan, at Gilgal beside the Jordan, in the land of the Israelites.
The whole congregation of the Israelites gathered at Shiloh to go to war against them.
The Israelites sent Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead,
with ten leaders accompanying him, one leader from each of the tribes of Israel. These men were heads of the military divisions of Israel.
They came to the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead. They spoke with them and said to them,

“This is what the whole assembly of the Lord says: What is this unfaithfulness you have committed against the God of Israel? You have turned away from following the Lord and built yourselves an altar to break away from the worship of the Lord.
Was the sin of Peor not enough for us? We have not cleansed ourselves from it to this day, and a plague came upon the assembly of the Lord.
If you turn away today from the worship of the Lord, tomorrow wrath will come upon the whole assembly of Israel.

But if the land of your inheritance is unclean, cross over to the land of the Lord’s inheritance, where the Lord’s tabernacle stands, and take an inheritance among us. Do not despise the worship of the Lord, and do not rebel against us by building yourselves an altar besides the altar of the Lord, the God of Israel.

Did you not see how Achan son of Carmi transgressed and took some of the things devoted to destruction, and wrath came upon the whole assembly of Israel? He was only one man, yet we all suffered because of his sin.”

The descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh answered and spoke with Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and with the heads of the military divisions of Israel. They said to them,

“The Lord is the God of gods; the God of gods is the Lord, and he is our God. He knows Israel, and he knows us. If we have done this to break away from him or to act unfaithfully in the worship of the Lord, may he not save us today.
If we have built ourselves an altar to turn away from the worship of the Lord, or to offer a sacrifice or any other worship upon it, may the Lord hold us accountable.
Rather, we did this out of fear of him, so that in the future your children would not say to our children, ‘What connection do you have with the Lord, the God of Israel?’

‘You descendants of Reuben and Gad, the Lord has placed this Jordan as a boundary between us and you. From now on you have no share in the Lord, the God of Israel.’ Then in the future your children would stop our children from fearing the Lord.
For this reason we said, “Let us make a place for ourselves and build an altar for ourselves, not for sacrifice and not for an offering.”

Rather, it is to be a witness between us and you and between our generations after us, that we and our generations after us serve the Lord before him with our burnt offerings, our sacrifices, and our offerings, in the place the Lord chooses for his name to dwell there, so that in the future your children will not say to our children, ‘You have no share in the Lord.’

And we said, ‘When they say this to us and to our generations in the future, they will say to them, “Look at the replica of the Lord’s altar that our ancestors made, not for burnt offerings or sacrifices, but to be a witness between us and you.”’

Far be it from us to reject the fear of the Lord and turn away from fearing the Lord, and to build ourselves an altar for burnt offerings, offerings, and sacrifices apart from the altar of the Lord, the God of Israel, that stands before his tabernacle.

Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the assembly, the heads of Israel’s forces who were with him, heard the words spoken by the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and they were pleased.

Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to the descendants of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh, ‘Today we know that the Lord is among us, because you have not committed this act of unfaithfulness against the Lord. You have now rescued the Israelites from having the Lord’s hand come against them in anger.’

Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders with him returned from the descendants of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh, from the land of Gilead to the land of Canaan, to the Israelites, and brought them back a report.
The report pleased the Israelites, and the Israelites blessed God. They no longer spoke of going to war against them to devastate the land where the descendants of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh lived.
The descendants of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh called the altar they had made ‘The Altar of Witness,’ because it was a witness between them that the Lord alone is God.
After many days, the Lord gave Israel rest from all their enemies around them, and Joshua had grown old and advanced in years.
Joshua summoned all Israel—its elders, its leaders, its judges, and its scribes—and said to them, ‘I have grown old and advanced in years.
You have seen everything the Lord your God did to all these nations, which he destroyed before you. The Lord your God himself fought your battles.

But see that I have not allotted to you these remaining nations as an inheritance for your tribes. From the Jordan, all the nations I destroyed, and the Great Sea toward the setting sun, I have allotted to you.
The Lord your God himself will break them and destroy them before you, and you will possess their land, as the Lord your God told you.
Only be very strong, and observe and do everything written in the book of the law of Moses, the Lord’s servant. Do not turn away from it to the right or to the left.
Do not mix with these nations that remain among you. Do not mention the names of their gods or swear by them. Do not serve them or bow down to them.
Instead, hold fast to the LORD your God, as you have done to this day.
The Lord destroyed great and powerful nations before you, and no one has stood against you to this day.
One man among you will pursue a thousand, because the Lord your God is with you, and he fights your battles, just as he told you.
Be very careful to fear the LORD your God.
But if you turn back and attach yourselves to the remnant of these nations that remain among you, intermarry with them, and mix with them and they with you,

know that the Lord your God will no longer destroy these nations before you. They will become snares and stumbling blocks for you, lashes against your sides and hooks in your eyes, until you perish from the good land that the Lord your God has given you.

As for me, I am now going the way of all the earth. You know with all your heart and all your soul that not one word has failed of all the good things the Lord your God said concerning you. They have all come upon you; not one word has failed.
But just as all the good things the Lord your God told you have come upon you, so all the curses will come upon you, until he destroys you from this good land that the Lord your God has given you.

If you violate the covenant of the LORD your God and the commandments you were given, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them, the anger of the LORD your God will burn against you, and you will quickly perish from the good land he has given you.
Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel at Shechem. He summoned the elders of Israel, their leaders, their judges, and their scribes, and stood before the tent of meeting, before God.
Joshua said to all the people, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Long ago your ancestors lived beyond the River—Terah, the father of Abraham and Nahor—and they served other gods there.
I took your father Abraham from beyond the River and led him throughout the land of Canaan. I multiplied his descendants and gave him Isaac.
I gave Isaac Jacob and Esau, and I gave Esau the hill country of Seir as an inheritance. But Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.
I sent Moses and Aaron, struck the Egyptians, and performed wonders among them. After that I brought you out.
I brought your ancestors out of Egypt and brought them to the sea. The Egyptians pursued your ancestors with chariots and horsemen to the Red Sea.

Your ancestors cried out to the LORD, and he placed darkness between them and the Egyptians. The LORD divided the Red Sea and brought your ancestors through it. He brought the sea over the Egyptians and covered them. Your own eyes saw what I did to the Egyptians. I brought you into the wilderness, and you lived in the wilderness for a long time.
You came to the land of the Amorites who lived beyond the Jordan. They fought against you, but I handed them over to you and destroyed them before you, and you took possession of their land.
Then Balak son of Zippor, king of the Moabites, rose up and fought against Israel. He sent for Balaam son of Beor to curse you.
But I was not willing to listen to Balaam. Instead, I surely blessed you and rescued you from his hands.

You crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The men of Jericho fought against you, along with the Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites, but I handed them over to you.
I sent hornets ahead of you and destroyed the two kings of the Amorites before you—not by your swords or your bows.
I gave you land on which you had not labored and towns you had not built, and you settled in them. Now you eat from vineyards and olive trees you did not plant.
Now fear the LORD and serve him with integrity and faithfulness. Remove from your hearts the foreign gods your ancestors served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve the LORD.

But if serving the LORD seems wrong to you, choose for yourselves today whom you will serve: the gods your ancestors served beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you live. But I and my household will serve the LORD, who is God.”
All the people answered, “Far be it from us to forsake the Lord and serve other gods!

“For the LORD is our God, the one who brought us up from the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery. He performed these great signs before us and protected us along the entire road we traveled and among all the peoples through whom we passed.

The LORD our God destroyed all these peoples, including the Amorites in whose land we live. The LORD destroyed them before us. Therefore we will serve the LORD, because he alone is God, and he is our God.”
Joshua said to the people, “Consider carefully whether you can serve the LORD, because he is a holy God and a jealous God. He will not forgive your offenses and your sins.
If you abandon the LORD and serve other, foreign gods of the land, the LORD will turn against you, bring disaster on you, and destroy you after having done you good.”
The people said to Joshua, “We will have no other worship; we worship the Lord God alone.”
Joshua said to the people, “You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen for yourselves to serve the LORD.” They said to him, “We are witnesses.”
Joshua said to them, “Now remove the foreign gods among you and direct your hearts toward the LORD, the God of Israel.”
The people said to Joshua, “We will serve the Lord our God and obey his voice.”
Joshua made a covenant with the people that day and taught them commandments and laws at Shechem.
Joshua wrote these words in the book of God's law. He took a large stone and set it up beneath the terebinth in the LORD's sanctuary.

Joshua said to all the people, “Look, this stone will be a witness for us, because it has heard all the words the LORD has spoken to us. It will be a witness against you, so that you do not deny the LORD your God.”
After Joshua had instructed the people, he sent them away, each to his own inheritance.
After these things, Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died at the age of one hundred and ten.
They buried him within the territory of his inheritance, at Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
Israel served the LORD throughout Joshua's lifetime and throughout the lifetimes of the elders who lived on after Joshua and knew the deeds the LORD had done for Israel.

The bones of Joseph, which the Israelites had brought up from Egypt, were buried at Shechem, in the plot of land Jacob had bought from Hamor, the father of Shechem, for a hundred ewes. It became an inheritance for Joseph's descendants.
Eleazar the priest, son of Aaron the priest, died, and they buried him on the hill of his son Phinehas, which had been given to him in the hill country of Ephraim.
